title: A History of God: The 4,000-Year Quest of Judaism, Christianity and Islam
author: Karen Armstrong
target_audience: General readers interested in the history of religion
Students and scholars of religious studies
Individuals curious about the development of monotheism
Those seeking an accessible overview of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam
core_themes: Development of the concept of God in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam
Relationship between religion, culture, and philosophy
Interpretation of scripture and religious experience
Interaction and influence between Abrahamic faiths
primary_purpose: To trace the historical evolution and transformation of the concept of God in the three major monotheistic faiths—Judaism, Christianity, and Islam—highlighting shared roots, divergent paths, common questions, and the impact of historical events and philosophical ideas on religious belief.

structure_format.narrative_style: Scholarly yet accessible, descriptive and analytical
structure_format.organization: Chronological approach, divided into major historical eras and religious/philosophical movements
features: Contextual explanation of key theological debates
Profiles of significant thinkers and prophets

key_concepts_lessons: The idea of God has continuously evolved, shaped by social, political, and philosophical changes.
Monotheistic religions share a complex and intertwined history.
God has been interpreted in diverse, sometimes conflicting ways even within single traditions.
Mysticism, philosophy, and rationalism have all played roles in shaping religious understanding.
Religion and the God concept respond to the intellectual and existential challenges of each era.
notable_features: Balanced treatment of Judaism, Christianity, and Islam
Uses both primary sources and modern scholarship
cultural_historical_context: Published at a time when interest in interfaith dialogue and understanding was increasing, especially after the end of the Cold War and in the context of global religious and political shifts. The book addresses the modern reader’s struggle with religious relevance in a secularizing world.
reception_impact: Became an international bestseller, translated into numerous languages
Praised for its depth, readability, and impartial approach
Regarded as a major work in popular religious studies
Helped to stimulate renewed academic and public interest in the roots of monotheism
Some critics questioned its theological depth or thought it painted traditions with a broad brush
comparable_titles: The Case for God by Karen Armstrong
God: A Human History by Reza Aslan
The Evolution of God by Robert Wright
The Great Transformation by Karen Armstrong
